analyst_view.overall: Hoffenheim (13th, 9 points) host Schalke (17th, 6 points), who are the Bundesliga's lowest scorers with four goals, have failed to score in their last four games and have gone six competitive matches without a win. Hoffenheim drew 1-1 with Crystal Palace in the Europa League on Thursday and have a long injury list (Hajdari, Hranáč, Gendrey, Conté, De Cat, Wimmer out; Coufal and Hložek face fitness checks). Schalke get Robin Gosens and Soufiane El-Faouzi back, but Wöber, Bachmann, Schallenberg, Gantenbein and Sylla are still missing.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.8 goals, already well below the league average because of Schalke's blunt attack. That fits the news: Schalke haven't scored in four games, and Hoffenheim are tired after Thursday's Europa League game and missing several attackers. One preview expects a 2-0 home win, which is close to the site's view, so we stay with it.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, mostly Hoffenheim's (7.7). Schalke's coach Miron Muslic talks about Hoffenheim's physical presence and intense pressing, and a home side chasing a low-scoring opponent tends to win corners. That is what the numbers already expect, so no change.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, already up because of referee Martin Petersen's record. Schalke are in the relegation zone, short of wins and under growing criticism, and Hoffenheim's press usually forces fouls from a side that struggles to play out. We lean slightly higher than the site.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with Hoffenheim taking 19. Hoffenheim played a full Europa League game on Thursday night with several attacking players unavailable (Hložek and Moerstedt among them), so their volume may dip a little. We lean slightly below the site's total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, with only 2.8 for Schalke. That matches a Schalke attack that has gone four games without a goal, and we found nothing that changes the Hoffenheim side, so we stay with the site.
